The effects of Y addition on microstructure and mechanical property of Nb-1Zr-0.1C alloy were investigated.
Y2O3 particles, with a size of approximately 2 µm, are distributed within the as-cast Nb-1Zr-0.1C alloy with 0.1Y and 0.4Y additions.
In the cold-rolled and annealed Nb-1Zr-0.1C alloy with 0.1 % Y addition, Y2O3 was continuously distributed along the grain boundaries of the Nb matrix that had undergone complete recrystallization.

After CR & A treatment, Y2O3 phase was continuously distributed along the grain boundaries in the Nb-1Zr-0.1C alloy with 0.1Y addition, contributing to the recrystallization of the Nb matrix during the annealing process.

the improvement in strength and plasticity of the warm-rolled and annealed Nb-1Zr-0.1C alloy with the addition of 0.4Y may be attributed to the larger number of Y2O3 particles that contribute to precipitation strengthening in materials.
This improvement may be attributed to the complete recrystallization of the Nb matrix and the continuous distribution of Y2O3 phase along the grain boundaries.
